project.name: Strapontin
project.description: Agrégateur de concerts personnel — suit artistes et salles, agrège Ticketmaster et Eventim, notifie par email et push

layers.name: Database Layer

layers.description: Shared pure-function business logic published as @strapontin/core: text normalisation, Levenshtein similarity, and the three-pass concert deduplication engine used by both the worker and web app.

layers.description: API client adapters published as @strapontin/sources that fetch concert data from Ticketmaster Discovery v2 and Eventim France, plus a MusicBrainz/Deezer canonical name resolver with Redis caching.

layers.description: BullMQ worker process that executes all background jobs (fetch concerts by artist/venue/region, recalculate user matches, send digest emails, send push notifications) and schedules them via a recurring cron.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Strapontin does and why it exists. It is an invite-only personal concert aggregator that fetches events from Ticketmaster and Eventim every 2 hours and notifies users by email or push notification. The README also sets out the fundamental architectural principle: all API calls happen in the background worker — the browser only ever reads the database. This single constraint drives every design decision in the codebase.

tour.title: Monorepo Structure
tour.description: The root `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` define the monorepo topology: three apps (`web`, `worker`) and two shared packages (`core`, `sources`) managed as a pnpm workspace with pnpm@11 pinned via corepack. Understanding this layout is essential — when you see `@strapontin/core` imported in the worker, you know it comes from `packages/core`. The `tsconfig.base.json` enforces strict TypeScript settings across all packages from a single source of truth.

tour.title: Database Schema
tour.description: The Drizzle ORM schema (`packages/core/src/schema.ts`) is the canonical source of truth for all 13 database tables and their TypeScript types. The initial migration (`0000_initial.sql`) creates the core data model: `concerts` (the central aggregation store), `users`, `user_artistes` and `user_salles` (what users follow), `user_matches` (which concerts match which user), and `user_config` (per-user preferences). Understanding these tables upfront makes every route and worker job immediately legible.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle ORM uses a code-first approach: `schema.ts` declares tables as TypeScript values, and `drizzle-kit generate` diffs the schema against the previous snapshot to produce a SQL migration. The inferred `$inferSelect` and `$inferInsert` types give you zero-boilerplate TypeScript types for each table row.

tour.title: Normalisation & Deduplication
tour.description: The `@strapontin/core` package provides the pure business logic shared by both `web` and `worker`. `normalisation.ts` strips accents, punctuation, and performs city-name substitutions (saint → st) to produce consistent keys. `deduplication.ts` then applies a three-pass algorithm on incoming concerts: exact match on `(artiste_norm, date, ville_norm)`, fuzzy match on `(date, ville_norm)` with Levenshtein similarity ≥ 0.85, and a venue-name fallback for cases where Ticketmaster and Eventim report different city names. This is the algorithmic core that makes cross-source aggregation reliable.
tour.languageLesson: Levenshtein distance measures the minimum number of single-character edits to transform one string into another. Normalising before comparing (removing accents, lowercasing) dramatically reduces false negatives; the 0.85 threshold allows for minor spelling differences between sources while avoiding false matches.

tour.title: External API Sources
tour.description: The `@strapontin/sources` package provides the two live data clients. `types.ts` defines the shared `ConcertBrut` DTO and the `SourceConcerts` interface that both clients implement. `ticketmaster.ts` calls the Discovery v2 API with quota tracking — every response includes a rate-limit header that the client parses and stores in Redis. `eventim.ts` uses a reverse-engineered internal Eventim API. `resolver.ts` canonicalises artist and venue names via MusicBrainz (then Deezer as a fallback) with a 7-day Redis cache, which is critical because Ticketmaster returns French venue names in ALL CAPS.

tour.title: Worker Entry Point & Job Scheduler
tour.description: `apps/worker/src/index.ts` is the background process entry point. It creates a BullMQ `Worker` with `concurrency: 2` (deliberately kept low to avoid TM rate-limit bursts) and registers `traiterJob` as the handler for all job types. A `setInterval` calls the scheduler every 2 hours. `cron.ts` implements the scheduler: it reads all users and their followed artists/venues from the database, then enqueues the appropriate fetch jobs, respecting two TM quota thresholds — if available quota falls below 500, batch cron jobs are skipped; below 50, all TM jobs abort.
tour.languageLesson: BullMQ uses Redis as its job store. Jobs with a fixed `jobId` are idempotent — adding the same job ID twice is a no-op. For recurring cron jobs this means using `removeOnComplete: true` (not `{ count: N }`) to clear the Redis hash after completion, otherwise re-queuing is silently ignored on subsequent scheduler runs.

tour.title: Job Execution & Concert Persistence
tour.description: `jobs.ts` implements the handler for every job type: `fetch:artiste`, `fetch:artistes:batch`, `fetch:region`, `fetch:salle`, `recalculer:matches`, `purger:concerts`, and `digest:quotidien`. After fetching raw concerts from the sources, each job calls through to `persister.ts`, which is the most logic-dense file in the worker. The persister reconciles venue names across sources, upserts concerts with diacritics and casing preference rules, then recalculates `user_matches` for all users, applying geographic department filters before triggering push and email notifications.

tour.title: Web Server Hooks & Authentication
tour.description: `hooks.server.ts` is the first file that runs on every SvelteKit request. It sequences three handlers: `bloquerAccesDirectIP` (rejects requests whose `Host` header is a bare IP address — guarding against direct-IP bypass of the nginx proxy), `securiser` (injects COOP, CORP, and X-Robots-Tag headers), and `gererAuth` (resolves the Better Auth session, writes user and theme to `event.locals`, redirects unauthenticated users, and enforces 2FA for admin accounts). `auth.ts` configures Better Auth with a Drizzle adapter, username plugin, TOTP two-factor plugin, and an after-hook that logs sign-in attempts to pino.
tour.languageLesson: SvelteKit's `handle` hook wraps every request/response cycle. Composing multiple handlers with `sequence(a, b, c)` from `@sveltejs/kit/hooks` keeps each concern independent and testable. Values written to `event.locals` in a hook are available to all `load` functions and `+server.ts` routes for that request.

tour.title: Shared Server Infrastructure
tour.description: Several singleton modules underpin all server routes. `db.ts` exports the Drizzle connection pool (fan-in: 7 — the most widely imported file in the project). `redis.ts` exports the ioredis client and key-name helpers, keeping all Redis key strings in one place. `queue.ts` exports the shared BullMQ `Queue` instance so web routes can enqueue background jobs (e.g., when a user adds an artist the `fetch:artiste` job is immediately enqueued). `config.ts` provides AES-256-GCM encrypted read/write access to the `app_config` table for API keys stored by the admin.

tour.title: Main App Routes
tour.description: The `(app)` route group is protected by its layout server, which redirects unauthenticated users to `/login`. The root page (`+page.server.ts`) queries `user_matches` joined with `concerts` to build the dashboard of matched concerts. The `/spectacles` route adds multi-filter support (month, genre, classification, source, price, status). The `/artistes` route loads followed artists and enqueues a `fetch:artiste` job on add. The `/salles` route does the same for venues. Together these routes show how every user interaction immediately triggers a background job rather than a synchronous API call.

tour.title: Frontend Shell & UI System
tour.description: The root layout (`+layout.svelte`) and authenticated layout (`(app)/+layout.svelte`) form the navigation shell. `BottomNav.svelte` serves mobile users; `Sidebar.svelte` serves desktop users. The design system is built on shadcn-svelte with Tailwind v4, configured via `components.json`. `app.html` contains an inline theme-detection script to apply the correct dark/light CSS class before the page paints, preventing flash of unstyled content. `app.css` defines the Tailwind base layers and CSS custom properties for the token system.

tour.title: PWA, Push Notifications & Service Worker
tour.description: Strapontin installs as a Progressive Web App. `manifest.json` declares the app name, icons, and standalone display mode. `service-worker.ts` pre-caches static assets and listens for push events from the server, showing a notification and handling `notificationclick` to open `/spectacles`. The `/api/push` route manages VAPID subscription registration and deletion (capped at 10 per user). The worker's `push.ts` reads subscriptions from `push_abonnements` and sends Web Push payloads via web-push, auto-cleaning expired subscriptions that return 404 or 410.
tour.languageLesson: Web Push uses VAPID (Voluntary Application Server Identification) to authenticate the push server. VAPID keys must be stable — changing them invalidates all existing browser subscriptions stored in `push_abonnements`. The GET `/api/push` endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so the service worker can retrieve the public key without a session cookie.

tour.title: CI/CD & Deployment Pipeline
tour.description: `.woodpecker.yaml` defines the three-step pipeline that runs on every push. The `test` step runs unit tests across all packages with mocked databases. The `typecheck` step runs `svelte-check`, `tsc --noEmit`, and `pnpm audit`. On merges to `main`, the `deploy` step SSHes into the production LXC and calls `update.sh`. That script orchestrates the full deployment sequence: `backup.sh` (pg_dump to NAS), `git reset --hard`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm build`, `drizzle-kit migrate`, `systemctl restart`, and finally a health-check against `/health` with 10 retries. A `trap ERR` provides automatic rollback if any step fails.
tour.languageLesson: YAML CI/CD pipelines use `depends_on` to serialize steps that share a resource. In this project the `typecheck` step depends on `test` to prevent both steps from running `pnpm install` on the same `.pnpm-store` directory simultaneously, which caused ENOENT race conditions on pnpm 11.
